summary: Cross-cloud impersonation proxy failing: AWS->GCP role chain blocked by org-policy/permission-boundary
description:
Issue summary: An internal debugging utility (impersonation-proxy) that performs a two-step cross-cloud impersonation (assume AWS role -> exchange STS creds for GCP workload-identity access) is failing with authorization errors when running from staging and intermittently in prod. Impact: Engineers cannot access cross-cloud logs and diagnostics; some automated oncall playbooks that require audit reads are blocked. Environment: staging us-west and prod us-east. Error snippets: 
- AWS side: 'AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole' returned intermittently for the ops-broker role.
- GCP side: 'Permission denied: iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy' and 'Request had insufficient authentication scopes' when the proxy attempts to impersonate target SA.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run impersonation-proxy from a workspace with the ops-aws-bridge role in account: redwood-infra-ops-prod.
2) Proxy attempts sts:AssumeRole to arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ops-broker-role.
3) On success, it exchanges temporary AWS creds with our sts-exchange lambda to mint a short-lived GCP access token via workload identity pool.
4) The final step attempts gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy for target-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and fails.

Observed behavior:
- Failure rate ~20% in prod, 100% in staging after maintenance window on 2026-03-09.
- Logs show both AWS AssumeRole errors and GCP IAM access errors; failures are correlated with recent org policy change and an automated permission-boundary rollout to some service accounts.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recently deployed permission boundary on ops-broker-role (AWS) blocks sts:TagSession or conditions used by the proxy causing intermittent AssumeRole failures.
- GCP failures stem from missing iam.serviceAccounts.actAs binding for the impersonation principal produced by the workload identity pool exchange, possibly because the GCP IAM binding was applied to a specific principal format that changed after the exchange implementation update.

Investigation notes:
- Checked Terraform diffs for the week of 2026-03-08: found PR #repo/infra/terraform/changesets/1248 that added a permission boundary to 'ops-broker-role' and tightened org-policy on 'iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' for staging.
- CloudTrail (aws-us-east-1) shows AssumeRole API returning AccessDenied with condition 'PermissionBoundaryEvaluationFailed' for three distinct sessions.
- GCP audit logs (projects/redwood-prod) show 'permission_denied' for service account getIamPolicy when principal is 'principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/12345/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/wip-prod/providers/p-ops#c9a8f2e2', suggesting the exchange step changed the principal format from 'serviceAccount:...'.
- Correlation: proxies that use the old exchange lambda version (v2.1) succeed; proxies that pick up the newer lambda (v3.0) produce the new principal format and fail because no IAM binding exists for that principal.

Temporary workaround:
- Roll back the sts-exchange lambda to v2.1 in staging to restore previous principal format (applied as hotfix on 2026-03-10).
- For AWS errors, granted a narrowly scoped sts:AssumeRole policy exception to the ops-broker-role for sessions originating from the proxy identity (timebound, expires 2026-03-17).

Resolution plan (in progress):
- Short term: Update IAM bindings in GCP to accept both principal formats used by v2.1 and v3.0 of the exchange lambda; coordinate with security to whitelist workload identity pool principals for the impersonation proxy.
- Mid term: Reconcile permission boundary policies in AWS to allow sts:AssumeRole with the required session tags and documented conditions for the proxy. Submit a follow-up Terraform PR that includes explicit allow statements for the proxy session tags and documents the rationale.
- Long term: Add an integration test that exercises the full assume-role -> workload-identity exchange workflow during CI to prevent format regressions.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Marco Ruiz: Create Terraform PR to add dual-format IAM bindings in GCP and run canary in staging (due 2026-03-15).
- Clara Nguyen (security): Approve narrow permission-boundary exception and review the fallback allow list (due 2026-03-12, extended).
- SRE runbook update: Add a diagnostic section for PermissionBoundaryEvaluationFailed and workload-identity principal mismatches.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Marco Ruiz: Confirmed staging proxies started failing right after infra TF apply. Captured CloudTrail events and GCP audit entries. Reverted lambda in staging as temporary measure.

2026-03-10 11:48 - Clara Nguyen (Security): Permission boundary change was intentional to reduce blast radius; however we can add an explicit allow for proxy session tags for a timebound window while we create a safer policy.

2026-03-11 15:02 - Aisha Patel: Ran targeted test that reproduces principal format mismatch. v2.1 produces 'serviceAccount:impersonator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'; v3.0 produces 'principal://iam.googleapis.com/...#c9a8f2e2'. Adding both to bindings resolves issue in staging.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Marco Ruiz: Opened terraform PR to add dual-format binding and documented the security rationale. Requesting security review and canary approval for 2026-03-14.

2026-03-13 10:45 - Clara Nguyen (Security): Reviewed PR, suggested reducing scope of binding to specific service accounts and adding audit-only policy first. Marked action items for next security committee meeting.
resolution: Partial: Hotfix rollback of exchange lambda (v2.1) in staging restored functionality. Narrow AWS sts:AssumeRole exception granted and dual-format GCP IAM binding PR opened. Awaiting security sign-off and a staged canary in prod. Full resolution pending policy reconciliation and CI integration test.
